title: GL period close
purpose: Closes a general-ledger period for one region: keeps the latest entry per account and day, runs a balance per account, and loads one row per account and period -- total, closing balance and entry count -- into GL_SUMMARY.

outputs.post_sql: UPDATE dbo.GL_SUMMARY SET LOADED_FLAG = 'Y' WHERE LOADED_FLAG IS NULL
outputs.grain: one row per account and period

columns.name: TOTAL
columns.meaning: Sum of the kept entries' AMOUNT for the account and period

columns.name: CLOSING_BAL
columns.meaning: Running balance of the account at its last entry in the period

columns.name: ENTRIES
columns.meaning: Number of kept entries (rows, whether or not they carry an ENTRY_ID)

columns.name: HAS_PERIOD_END
columns.meaning: Y when any kept entry was posted on the period-end date, otherwise N

columns.name: LOADED_FLAG
columns.meaning: Set to Y by the PostSQL on rows that have none yet; not written by the summary itself, so NULL on a row the run inserted until the PostSQL runs

steps.name: Extract the region's ledger entries
steps.does: Reads GL_LEDGER (the source query keeps only rows whose AMOUNT is not 0), keeps the run's region (the workflow constant User.Region, EMEA) and parses POSTED from dd/mm/yyyy text into a date-time (POSTED_DT).

steps.name: Keep the latest entry per account and day
steps.does: Sorts by ACCT, POSTED_DT ascending and ENTRY_ID descending, then keeps the first row for each ACCT and POSTED_DT, which is the one with the largest ENTRY_ID.

steps.name: Running balance and period-end flag
steps.does: Adds a running balance (RUN_BAL) per account in that order, numbers the rows (RecordID) and flags the postings made on the period-end date (the constant User.PeriodEnd, 2026-08-31) in PERIOD_END_FLAG.

steps.name: Close the period and load GL_SUMMARY
steps.does: Summarizes per ACCT and PERIOD (total AMOUNT, the last RUN_BAL as the closing balance, the entry count, whether any posting is on the period-end date); deletes GL_SUMMARY rows before 2020-01, merges the summary in on ACCT and PERIOD, and then sets LOADED_FLAG to Y where it is still NULL.

rules: Only the ledger rows of the run's region (User.Region, EMEA) are used.
Rows whose AMOUNT is 0 or NULL never reach the workflow: the source query drops them.
When an account has several entries on one day, only the one with the largest ENTRY_ID is kept.
CLOSING_BAL is the running balance on the last row of the account and period in the order the rows are numbered after the sort.
GL_SUMMARY is updated, not replaced: a row with the same ACCT and PERIOD is overwritten, a new one is inserted and every other row stays exactly as it was.
Before the load, GL_SUMMARY rows with PERIOD earlier than 2020-01 are deleted; after it, LOADED_FLAG is set to Y wherever it is still NULL.
HAS_PERIOD_END is Y when any kept entry of the account and period was posted on the period-end date.

parity_risks.note: The Input tool's own query carries `WHERE AMOUNT <> 0`. The translation reads the mapped table rather than running that query, so the predicate has to be written out again; without it every zero or NULL amount would reach the rest of the workflow, which Alteryx never saw.

Filter [REGION] = [User.Region]: a NULL REGION makes the expression NULL, and Alteryx sends both false AND NULL to the False anchor. That anchor is not wired, so those rows simply leave the workflow -- which is also what a three-valued SQL WHERE does with them.

[User.Region] is a workflow constant, not a column. Its value ('EMEA') is resolved at translation time into a literal; nothing at run time supplies it, and a run wanting another region needs a new translation.

The DateTime tool reads dd/mm/yyyy text and writes NULL for text the format cannot read, so TRY_TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ (not TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ) is the warn-and-null form; 31/02/2026 is the row that proves it.
POSTED_DT is an Alteryx DateTime, so a parsed date carries midnight: the column is TIMESTAMP_NTZ, not DATE, and comparing it against a DATE would be a type difference.
The Sort is not cosmetic: tools 5, 6, 7 and 9 all read its row order. NULL sorts first ascending and last descending, so every window's ORDER BY spells the NULLS placement out.

Unique keeps the FIRST row of each (ACCT, POSTED_DT) in incoming order, and incoming order is the Sort's ENTRY_ID DESC, so the surviving duplicate is the one with the LARGEST ENTRY_ID. A row number taken in any other order changes which row's AMOUNT reaches the Summarize.
Unique compares key values exactly, and two NULL POSTED_DT rows of the same ACCT count as the same key. PARTITION BY treats NULLs as one group, which is the same rule.

RUN_BAL is a Double field, so the model adds the exact decimal amounts and converts to a binary double when it stores each row. The translation sums the NUMBER column in a window and casts once, which agrees for every amount in the golden sets; a running total long enough to lose a double's precision would not.

Record ID numbers rows in incoming order, so its value depends entirely on the Sort. It never reaches the target -- the Summarize drops it -- but CLOSING_BAL is defined as the last row by that number, so ordering.order_dependent_columns names CLOSING_BAL.
IIF's condition is NULL when POSTED_DT is NULL, and a NULL condition takes the else branch in both Alteryx and SQL, so those rows are flagged 'N' rather than NULL.
Alteryx's Count counts ROWS, not values, so ENTRIES is COUNT(*) and the edge set's NULL-ENTRY_ID row still counts as one.

Last takes the group's last row in incoming order, including a NULL. There is no ordered aggregate for it in either dialect, so the translation takes the value at the largest RECORD_ID; that is the same row as long as RECORD_ID is unique, which it is because it is a row number.

Update; Insert if new maps columns to the target by NAME and writes only the six the Summarize produces. LOADED_FLAG is left untouched on a matched row and arrives NULL on an inserted one, which is precisely what the PostSQL then fills. A NULL update key matches nothing, so the edge set's NULL-ACCT group is inserted rather than merged.

The golden output is the target's state AFTER PreSQL, write and PostSQL -- not this run's rows. A row the run does not touch (9999) stays exactly as it was, and PERIOD < '2020-01' is deleted before anything is written.
